_about: Arthur Ransome (1884-1967): his own books, US public domain only. Anything first published in 1930 or earlier is US public domain today; each later book becomes free in the US on 1 January of its publication year + 96 (95-year term; foreign works restored by the URAA whether or not renewed), and the books first published after his death have their own dates. The full list with dates is _pending here and docs/RANSOME-SCHEDULE.md. US STATUS ONLY: Ransome died in 1967, so in the UK, the EU and other life+70 countries everything he wrote is in copyright until 2038-01-01 (see _jurisdiction). His translations and retellings of others (Old Peter's Russian Tales, Gourmont's A Night in the Luxembourg) are on lane C's ransome-translations shelf, not here. This shelf merges lane B's Swallows and Amazons entry (relay b69f8a0e, the 1946 Cape impression as raw OCR) with PR #21's Standard Ebooks text, which is the reading text; owner since 2026-10-10: the Ransome thread (PR #21), by the coordinator's assignment. Standard Ebooks texts are keyed from later printings with modernized spelling; see _rights_checked and _collation. Internet Archive items are raw, unproofread OCR (the Edwards precedent).

_jurisdiction.rule: the hosted chest is in the US and the US rule binds (as on the Chesterton and Barrie shelves). A work first published abroad in 1930-1977 has a US term of 95 years from publication (its copyright was restored by the URAA on 1996-01-01 whether or not it was ever renewed), so it is free on 1 January of the 96th year.
_jurisdiction.us: every book first published 1930 or earlier: public domain now. Every later one: see _pending.
_jurisdiction.uk_eu_life_plus_70: in copyright until 2038-01-01 (Ransome d. 1967-06-03). Armarium must not serve this text to readers in those countries if it ever serves by region.
_jurisdiction.canada: public domain since 2018-01-01 (life+50 for authors who died before 1972; Canada's 2022 extension to life+70 is not retroactive). This is why Faded Page holds all twelve; a Canadian transcription is not US public domain for that reason.
_jurisdiction.illustrations: not taken: the pipeline is text only. The 1930 first edition carried only Steven Spurrier's endpaper maps and frontispiece (SE keeps those). Clifford Webb's drawings (1931) and Ransome's own (1938) are later publications with their own US dates (2027 and 2034).

ransome-aladdin.author: Title page read 2026-10-10: the OCR prints the author line as 'BY ARTHUR RANSONE' (an OCR slip for Ransome); the catalogue gives Nisbet, 1919, and the title words match.

_rights_checked.ransome-swallows-and-amazons: Kept as a later-printing, spelling-modernized witness of the 1930 text (the same class as the reprint questions in DIGEST-B; Adam's ruling on that class covers this one too). Standard Ebooks' imprint says the source text is believed US public domain and dedicates SE's work to CC0. No textual collation of the 1930 first edition against later printings has been published and no scan of the first edition is open online, so 'no revision' is inferred, not proved: see _collation.
_rights_checked.ransome-swallows-and-amazons-1930: Title page read 2026-10-10: 'London - JONATHAN CAPE - Toronto. FIRST PUBLISHED AUGUST 1930. NEW ILLUSTRATED EDITION 1931 ... TWENTY-THIRD IMPRESSION FEBRUARY 1946', 'Illustrated by the Author'. The text is Ransome's 1930 book, US public domain since 2026-01-01 (published 1930, 95-year term). US ONLY: Ransome died 1967, so it is under copyright in the UK and other life+70 countries until 2038. Two caveats awaiting Adam (DIGEST-B): this is a later printing and the text has not been collated against a 1930 copy; and Ransome's own drawings, whose captions may appear in the OCR, date from the 1938 edition, so those captions are not yet US public domain. Stated by hand because the gate is fail-closed at 1930. Kept 2026-10-10 as a raw collation witness beside the Standard Ebooks reading text (ransome-swallows-and-amazons); the slug is lane B's and is kept so its references resolve, though the scan is the 1946 impression, not 1930.
_rights_checked.ransome-letter-to-america: Read 2026-10-10: the pamphlet prints 'Reprinted from The New Republic of July 27, 1918' and is dated Moscow, May 14th, 1918; the catalogue record has no date, so the gate asks. Published 1918: US public domain.
_rights_checked.ransome-racundras-first-cruise: Standard Ebooks production (CC0) of the 1923 book; US public domain by date. Spelling may be modernized, as with all SE texts.

_collation.method: SE's chapters 1-31, lower-cased, to-day/to-morrow/to-night joined, compared word by word (difflib) with the raw OCR of two Cape printings on archive.org; counts only, no text kept
_collation.swallows-and-amazons_1946: archive.org 'swallows-and-amazons' (Cape, 'new illustrated edition 1931', 23rd impression Feb 1946): 101,020 of SE's 102,161 words match (98.9%); the rest is unseparated OCR noise, running heads and plate captions. This printing still has 'to-day' (25), 'to-morrow' (40), 'to-night' (7); SE has none and prints today/tomorrow/tonight instead.
_collation.dli.ernet.425473_1953: archive.org 'dli.ernet.425473' (Cape, 'this edition 1953'; the catalogue's 1930 is the first-publication year, not this printing): 98,872 of SE's words match (96.8%). This printing already reads 'today' (25) and 'tomorrow' (39): Cape's own resetting dropped the hyphens, so the modern spelling may be Cape's, not SE's.
